- Find safe shelter right away.
- Don't walk, swim, or drive through flood waters. Turn Around, Don't Drown!
- Remember, just six inches of moving water can knock you down, and one foot can sweep your vehicle away.
- Stay off bridges over fast-moving water.
- Depending on the type of flooding, evacuate if told to do so.
- Move to higher ground or a higher floor.

simplified: For many years, the farthest start of the Apurímac River on a big mountain in Peru was thought to be the most far. But in 2014, a study said the farthest start was actually the Mantaro River on a mountain range in Peru. These two rivers join with other smaller rivers to make the Ucayali River. This big river meets the Marañón River before reaching Iquitos, Peru. Many countries think this is the main part of the Amazon. But Brazilians call this part the Solimões River, which flows into another river called the Rio Negro near a big city in Brazil called Manaus.
note: BORDERLINE: first sentence garbled ("thought to be the most far") but no fact changed

simplified: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's biggest coral reef system with over 2,900 reefs and 900 islands stretching for about 2,300 km. It's near Queensland, Australia, between the coast and a channel about 160 km wide, about 61 m deep. You can see it from space. It's like a huge underwater structure made by tiny living things called coral polyps. This reef helps many different plants and animals live. It was named a World Heritage Site in 1981. CNN called it one of the Seven Natural Wonders in 1997. Australia put it on its list of World Heritage sites in 2007. Queensland's National Trust named it a special place in 2006.
note: BORDERLINE: "between the coast and a channel" garbles the location

simplified: Photosynthesis is how plants, algae, and cyanobacteria use light to make food. They have special parts called photopigments. These autotrophs (self-feeders) turn light into energy stored in sugars and other stuff inside them. When they need energy, they use it. This makes oxygen, which is important for breathing. Plants make most of the oxygen in the air.

simplified:
Remember fires are serious. Escape plans help you get out fast. Practice your plan twice a year. Think of firefighters as helpers, not people who catch you. Here are some ideas:
- Find two ways out of each room, in case the main way is blocked by fire or smoke.
- Make sure windows are not stuck, you can take out screens quickly, and security bars can be opened easily.
- Practice waking up in the dark or with your eyes closed.
- Teach kids not to hide. They should tell firefighters they're okay.
- Keep your bedroom door closed when sleeping.
note: NATURAL: adds "Think of firefighters as helpers…" and "They should tell firefighters they're okay"; "Practice waking up in the dark" for "feeling your way out"

simplified: A black hole is a very tiny thing that pulls in everything, even light. Albert Einstein's theory of how things move and bend space says anything very tiny will form a black hole. The edge where nothing can escape is called event horizon. Crossing this edge traps stuff inside but doesn't change things. It also says every black hole has a center where space bends really bad.
note: BORDERLINE NATURAL: "a very tiny thing" / "anything very tiny will form a black hole" vs "so compact"

simplified: In money stuff, inflation is when prices of things go up. It used to mean making more money. More money can make prices go up for everyone. We measure this with a price list, like the Consumer Price Index. When prices go up, you can buy less with your money. That’s called inflation. The opposite is when prices go down. That’s called deflation. The main way to see if prices are going up is the inflation rate, which is how much prices change each year.

simplified: Mount Vesuvius erupted in 79 AD. It destroyed Roman cities like Pompeii, Herculaneum, Oplontis, and Stabiae along with other places. Ejecting rocks, ash, and gases up to 33 km (21 miles), it sent molten rock and crushed bits of rock at 6,000,000 cubic metres (7,800,000 cubic yards) per second. About 1,000 people died, but we're not sure. The only record is two letters from Pliny the Younger to historian Tacitus.

simplified: Type 2 diabetes is a type of diabetes that makes your blood sugar high. It happens when your body can't use insulin well and sometimes doesn't make enough. Symptoms are thirst, needing to pee often, feeling tired, and losing weight. Other signs are being really hungry, having sore spots that take time to heal. These signs come slowly. Long-term, it can cause heart problems, strokes, eye problems that might make you go blind, and weak legs that might need amputations. Sometimes, blood sugar gets really high suddenly, but usually, it doesn't cause bad smells in the body.
note: NATURAL: "usually, it doesn't cause bad smells in the body" for "ketoacidosis is uncommon"
